The European Union plans to implement restrictions on social media access for children under 15 across its member states, aimed at enhancing child safety and wellbeing online. The legislation, dubbed the EU Kids Act, would prohibit anyone under 13 from accessing social media and limit users aged 13 to 15 to one hour of daily access through parental accounts. Member states would be required to enforce these rules once the act is approved, which would also mandate social media companies to submit detailed safety plans or face significant fines.

 - The EU Kids Act seeks to restrict social media access for children under 15 to improve online safety.
 - Social media companies will need to demonstrate the safety of their platforms or face fines.
